events.objective: Establish the exact symptom onset and blast radius. Query logs and metrics from ~14:30Z to 16:59Z for payment-service AND its likely collaborators (ledger-service, ledger DB/write path, message queue if any): (1) when did payment-service error rate first exceed baseline, and does that precede or follow the 15:10Z-reported onset; (2) is the 60% error rate isolated to payment-service or do ledger-service and other callers of the ledger write path show the same signature; (3) extract the exact error signatures/stack traces for ledger write failures (validation rejection vs timeout vs connection error vs 5xx from dependency); (4) trend resource metrics (latency, connection pool, CPU, disk) on the ledger write path. Report concrete evidence, not summaries.

Map what changed and what depends on what, across ALL services — not just payment-service. (1) List all deployments and config changes from 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-01T16:59Z with timestamps, including anything released around or shortly before the failure window, not only payment-service v6.0.0; (2) map payment-service's dependency graph and identify shared components (ledger-service, shared DB/migration, schema registry, feature flags) used by other services; (3) search historical incidents for prior 'new ledger entry type' / schema-rejection / payment-mandate failures and how they were resolved. Flag any change that is a stronger temporal candidate than v6.0.0.

Correlate the change timeline from task b against the precise onset time and error signature from task a: determine which single change (or change combination) aligns with onset within minutes, and whether the failing component is where the change was made. Specifically assess whether ledger write failures are caused by payment-service v6.0.0 itself, by a concurrent change in a dependency/shared component, or by a dependent config/schema change rejecting the new entry type. State the most likely root-cause component and recommended rollback/fix target, and note any evidence that rolling back payment-service alone would NOT fix it.

events.statement: payment-service error_rate jumped from a <1% baseline to ~60.5% at the 1-minute bucket 15:00:00Z (0.21% at 14:59, 60.5% at 15:00), with sustained ~59-67% values after; the earlier 5-min series shows the last normal bucket at 14:55 (avg 0.18) then 61.52 at 15:00:00Z.

Onset precedes the reported 15:10Z onset by ~10 minutes; the error rate was already ~60% in the 15:00Z bucket and roughly flat at 60-64% from 15:00 to 15:10Z, so the report's timing is late relative to the data.
payment-service logs show a single dominant error pattern: 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device', 354 ERROR entries, first_seen 2026-06-01T15:00:26Z.

ledger-db (the ledger write-path datastore; 'ledger-service' does not exist as a monitored service) logged disk-full failures beginning 15:01:01Z: 153x 'PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.<n>": No space left on device' and 139x 'could not extend file "base/<n>/<n>": No space left on device'.

ledger-db showed a disk-capacity warning before the outage: 14:48:20Z 'disk usage 98% on /var/lib/postgresql/data', plus an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining growing WAL (33916 MB at 14:34:05Z -> 69518 MB at 14:46:32Z -> 77371 MB at 14:49:47Z).

The failure mode is a storage/ENOSPC write failure at the database layer, not a validation rejection, timeout, connection error, or 5xx-from-dependency: both payment-service and ledger-db report 'No space left on device' on the ledger write path.

ledger-db is a shared postgres (owner platform, shared=true) with FOUR services writing to it: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; payment-service also depends on kafka (shared, queue-produce) and the external bank-partner-api (no telemetry). ledger-db is therefore a shared component through which a neighbour (e.g. settlement-service, order-service) could hurt payment-service.

Historical precedent HIST-114 (2025-04-18) is the closest match to 'ledger write failures': ledger-db 'disk full from retained WAL', symptoms 'no space left on device' / 'write failures', caused by an inactive replication slot retaining WAL, resolved by dropping the slot. HIST-111 (2025-05-22) shows a reporting query slowing ledger-db; HIST-102 (2025-09-02) shows portfolio-service timeouts during a ledger-db failover.

A prior payment-service failure HIST-105 (2025-11-19) had the same surface symptom set ('payment failures', 'bank api errors') but a dependency_failure root cause: the bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes. bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so this path is unverifiable from telemetry. This is a lead only, not evidence about INC-012.

events.statement: The entire window 2026-05-31T00:00Z-2026-06-01T16:59Z contains exactly one deployment AND zero config changes: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203) at 2026-06-01T14:46:00Z, status 'rolled_back' at 15:12:00Z, adding 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD' and 'mandate create/approve endpoints'. So the only change-combination candidate is v6.0.0 itself; no concurrent dependency-side deploy or flag change exists in the timeline.

v6.0.0 deployed at 14:46:00Z, i.e. ~14 min BEFORE the 15:00:26Z first 'ledger write failed: ... No space left on device' error and ~17 min before ledger-db's 15:01:01Z PANIC. The change therefore cannot be a >15-min-after causal agent; it is temporally upstream of onset within minutes-to-tens-of-minutes, consistent with a change that accelerates an existing resource drain.

The failing component is ledger-db, a SHARED postgres (owner platform, shared=true) written by FOUR services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service (callers via api-gateway). Its error signature is storage exhaustion ('No space left on device' on pg_wal/xlogtemp and base files), not a schema/validation rejection of the new MANDATE_HOLD entry type and not a timeout or 5xx-from-dependency - so the failure is not generated by payment-service's code path itself.

Pre-onset resource evidence on the shared datastore: ledger-db disk warning at 14:48:20Z ('disk usage 98%') and an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining growing WAL (33916 MB -> 69518 MB -> 77371 MB); at 14:48Z disk was already 98% full, 12 min before the outage, so the resource was near-exhaustion before/independently of the v6.0.0 deploy's steady-state traffic.

Historical precedent HIST-114 (2025-04-18, match_score 10) is the closest structural match: 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL', symptoms 'no space left on device'/'write failures', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'. This is a lead for the fix target (ledger-db slot/WAL), not evidence about INC-012's cause.

Rollback-alone insufficiency: payment-service v6.0.0 was already rolled back at 15:12:00Z, and a query for ANY payment-service deployment after 15:00Z returns count 0 - i.e. nothing was re-released and the affected service is sitting on the rolled-back state, yet the incident persisted to the 16:59Z data end. Combined with the shared-datastore failure mode, a payment-service-only rollback does not clear the ledger-db full disk that four services depend on.

events.description: No telemetry interval/query was available to me to confirm whether payment-service error_rate returned to baseline AFTER the 15:12:00Z rollback (agent T1's metrics only cover onset; I could not query metrics directly). This limits the claim that rollback alone failed to restore service - I can only show the rollback happened and no new deploy followed.

ledger-db's own deployment/config history is not exposed (only 1 deployment total in window, all payment-service), so I cannot confirm whether the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot or a retention setting was itself recently changed.
bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false (per T2 graph) and I could not query it; HIST-105 shows the same payment-failure surface symptom with a bank-API 5xx cause, an unverifiable alternative path.

events.answer: Timeline correlation points to the failing component NOT being where the change was made: the single change in the window (payment-service v6.0.0, deployed 14:46:00Z) sits ~14 min before the 15:00:26Z ENOSPC onset, but the error signature is a storage-exhaustion failure of the SHARED ledger-db (disk 98% at 14:48:20Z, WAL retained by inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot up to 77371 MB, "No space left on device" on pg_wal/xlogtemp from 15:01:01Z). v6.0.0 is the only change and therefore the most likely TRIGGER (MANDATE_HOLD writes accelerate WAL growth on an already ~98%-full volume), but the ROOT-CAUSE COMPONENT is ledger-db (WAL/disk + replication slot), not payment-service. Recommended fix target = ledger-db: drop/inactivate the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot to release the 34-77 GB of retained WAL (HIST-114 resolution) and/or expand the volume, then restore payment-service. Rolling back payment-service alone would NOT fix it: it was rolled back at 15:12:00Z, AFTER the 15:00Z onset, and post-rollback the affected service has zero deployments (tc-021) - i.e. no new version replaced the rollback - while the failures are produced by ledger-db's full disk shared by four writers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service).

events.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from retained WAL (inactive replication slot) is the origin; payment-service v6.0.0 is a coincidental accelerator/victim
payment-service v6.0.0's new MANDATE_HOLD write pattern accelerated disk/WAL consumption on ledger-db until it filled
A schema/contract change (migration, validation config, or flag) rejects the new MANDATE_HOLD entry type and breaks ledger writes
External bank-partner-api dependency failure is the origin; payment failures are the surface symptom (unverifiable)

tasks.answer: Timeline correlation points to the failing component NOT being where the change was made: the single change in the window (payment-service v6.0.0, deployed 14:46:00Z) sits ~14 min before the 15:00:26Z ENOSPC onset, but the error signature is a storage-exhaustion failure of the SHARED ledger-db (disk 98% at 14:48:20Z, WAL retained by inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot up to 77371 MB, "No space left on device" on pg_wal/xlogtemp from 15:01:01Z). v6.0.0 is the only change and therefore the most likely TRIGGER (MANDATE_HOLD writes accelerate WAL growth on an already ~98%-full volume), but the ROOT-CAUSE COMPONENT is ledger-db (WAL/disk + replication slot), not payment-service. Recommended fix target = ledger-db: drop/inactivate the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot to release the 34-77 GB of retained WAL (HIST-114 resolution) and/or expand the volume, then restore payment-service. Rolling back payment-service alone would NOT fix it: it was rolled back at 15:12:00Z, AFTER the 15:00Z onset, and post-rollback the affected service has zero deployments (tc-021) - i.e. no new version replaced the rollback - while the failures are produced by ledger-db's full disk shared by four writers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service).
